title: Molecular evolution of the Angiotensin II receptors AT1 and AT2: Specificity of the sodium binding site in amniota
authors: Asma Tiss; Rym Ben Boubaker; Daniel Henrion; Hajer Guissouma; Marie Chabbert
one_liner_zh: 该文通过系统发育、静电计算和MD模拟研究AT1/AT2受体钠结合位点的分子进化，虽涉及蛋白-配体（AngII肽）互作与MD方法，但对象为GPCR-肽配体而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题TF-DNA结合机制无直接关联。
abstract: In vertebrates, the octopeptide angiotensin II (AngII) is an important in vivo regulator of the cardiovascular system. It acts mainly through two G protein-coupled receptors, AT1 and AT2. To better understand the interplay between these receptors throughout the evolution of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS), we combined a phylogenetic study to electrostatics computations and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of AT1 and AT2 receptors from different species. The phylogenetic analysis reveals a mirror evolution of AT1 and AT2 that are both split in two clades, separating fish from terrestrian receptors. It also indicates that the unusual allosteric sodium binding site of human AT1 is specific of amniota. Other AT1 and AT2 receptors display a canonical sodium binding site with a serine at position 7.46 (Ballesteros numbering). Electrostatics computations and MD simulations support maintained sodium binding to human AT1 with ingress from the extracellular side. Comparison of the sodium binding modes in AT1 and AT2 from humans and eels indicates that the allosteric control by sodium in both AT1 and AT2 evolved during the transition from an aqueous to a terrestrial environment. The unusual S7.46N mutation in amniota AT1 is mirrored by a L3.36M mutation in amniota AT2. The S7.46N mutation increases the specificity of AT1 for AngII relative to Ang derivatives, whereas the L3.36M mutation might have the opposite effect on AT2. Both mutations should contribute to the split of the renin-angiotensin system into the classical (AngII/AT1) and counter-regulatory (Ang1-7/AT2, Mas) arms in amniota. AUTHOR SUMMARY The analysis of protein sequences from different species can reveal interesting trends in the structural and functional evolution of a protein family. Here, we analyze the evolution of two G protein-coupled receptors, AT1 and AT2, which bind the angiotensin II peptide and are important regulators of the cardiovascular system. We show that these receptors underwent a mirror evolution and that specific mutations of the sodium binding pocket in both AT1 and AT2 occurred in amniota. We underwent electrostatics computations and molecular dynamics simulations to decipher the details of the sodium binding mode in eel and human receptors, as prototype of fish and amniota receptors. Our results suggest that evolution favored an increased specificity of AT1 and a decreased specificity of AT2 for angiotensin II as compared to its derivatives. In turn, these data suggest that mutations in the sodium binding pocket of G protein-coupled receptors might be an efficient way to gain functional evolution.
abstract_zh: 在脊椎动物中，八肽血管紧张素II（AngII）是心血管系统的重要体内调节因子。它主要通过两种G蛋白偶联受体AT1和AT2发挥作用。为了更好地理解肾素-血管紧张素系统（RAS）进化过程中这些受体之间的相互作用，我们结合了系统发育研究、静电计算以及不同物种AT1和AT2受体的分子动力学（MD）模拟。系统发育分析揭示了AT1和AT2的镜像进化，两者均分为两个分支，将鱼类受体与陆生受体区分开来。分析还表明，人类AT1中不寻常的变构钠结合位点是羊膜动物特有的。其他AT1和AT2受体则表现出典型的钠结合位点，在7.46位（Ballesteros编号）含有丝氨酸。静电计算和分子动力学模拟支持人类AT1维持钠结合，且钠从细胞外侧面进入。对人类和鳗鱼AT1及AT2中钠结合模式的比较表明，AT1和AT2中钠的变构控制在从水生环境向陆生环境过渡期间发生了进化。羊膜动物AT1中特有的S7.46N突变与羊膜动物AT2中的L3.36M突变相对应。S7.46N突变增加了AT1对AngII相对于Ang衍生物的特异性，而L3.36M突变可能对AT2产生相反效果。这两种突变可能共同促进了肾素-血管紧张素系统在羊膜动物中分裂为经典（AngII/AT1）和反向调节（Ang1-7/AT2, Mas）两条通路。作者总结：对不同物种蛋白质序列的分析可以揭示蛋白质家族结构和功能进化中的有趣趋势。在此，我们分析了两种G蛋白偶联受体AT1和AT2的进化，它们结合血管紧张素II肽，是心血管系统的重要调节因子。我们表明，这些受体经历了镜像进化，并且在羊膜动物中，AT1和AT2的钠结合口袋发生了特定突变。我们进行了静电计算和分子动力学模拟，以解析鳗鱼和人类受体（分别作为鱼类和羊膜动物受体的原型）中钠结合模式的细节。我们的结果表明，进化倾向于增加AT1对血管紧张素II相对于其衍生物的特异性，同时降低AT2的特异性。反过来，这些数据表明，G蛋白偶联受体钠结合口袋中的突变可能是实现功能进化的有效途径。
